rule.borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are the ones where the two readings genuinely compete. Every one carries the reasoning that decided it, so a human can flip it and rerun.
rule.not_scheme: the money runs, builds, staffs or maintains an organisation or an asset, devolves general purpose funds to another tier of government, pays for the capacity of the delivery system rather than the benefit, discharges the state's obligation to its own serving or retired staff, or is an accounting or adjustment head
rule.scheme: the money buys an identifiable benefit received by a person or household: cash, a kit, food, a scholarship, a fee waiver, a pension, insurance, a subsidy, a loan, free supply, a house, land, treatment for a named beneficiary class, or training in which the trainee is himself the beneficiary
rule.the_line_that_did_the_work: Kerala's Annual Plan lists institutions beside schemes, so the first line is the obvious one: the Kerala Agricultural University, the State Institute of Languages, Bharat Bhavan, the Kerala State Chalachitra Academy and 44 wildlife sanctuaries and national parks are budget provisions and are not schemes. The line that actually cost the labelling time is the second one. A DEPARTMENTAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME IS NOT A SCHEME UNLESS THE STATE'S OWN WORDS SAY THE MONEY REACHES A PERSON. Kerala's plan is full of rows called Hi-Tech Agriculture, Soil Health Management and Productivity Improvement, Extension Forestry, Mariculture Activities and Development of Crops through Integrated Farming System Approach. Every one of them probably does pay a subsidy to some cultivator, and none of them says so. They are labelled not_scheme and flagged borderline, and the rule is stated here rather than applied silently: the name or the objectives sentence must name a transfer, a subsidy, an assistance, an incentive, a supply, a scholarship, a pension, a loan, insurance, food, housing, treatment or training given to a class of persons, or the row must name a programme whose defined content is such a transfer. A centrally sponsored mission with published per-beneficiary assistance norms counts under that second clause and a state programme with no stated recipient does not, which is why the National Food Security Mission rows are schemes and Hi-Tech Agriculture is not.
rule.the_second_line: An engagement by the state is not a benefit from the state. The honorarium to counsellors in tribal hostels, the allowances to care providers in Social Justice institutions, the training of ICDS functionaries and the life and accident insurance premium for anganwadi workers and helpers are all money reaching identifiable households, and all are labelled not_scheme because the state pays them as the employer or engager of its own scheme staff. This is the same line Tamil Nadu drew and it produces one of the surviving errors here, at score 8.

sampling: Stratified by sector family (WELFARE, SERVICE, ECONOMY, INFRA, GOVERNANCE, a fixed partition of the 50 scheme-code prefixes listed in parse/classify_kerala.py) crossed with allocation band (no figure, nil, and quartiles of the 1,893 rows that carry a positive allocation), 27 non-empty strata. The axis is the code prefix and not the printed sector string: the prefix is Kerala's own sector code, it is present and well formed on all 2,629 rows, and the printed sector carries 79 distinct values including TOTAL, (KILA), (100% CSS) and '(60% - Mission (Urban) 2.0 2217-05-191-48', which are page artefacts. The 50 prefixes cannot each be a stratum: 50 crossed with 6 bands is 300 cells and a sample large enough to fill them could not be labelled by hand. nil and 'no figure' are separate bands because the source keeps them separate: 733 rows are printed with a figure of zero, which is the state saying the scheme exists and is funded at nil, and 3 rows carry no figure at all. Within a stratum rows are sorted by key and picked at even spacing, so the sample is reproducible without a random seed. Allocation is proportional to stratum size with a floor of 4, so the sample is close to self weighting; stratum_size and stratum_sampled are carried on every stratified row so a weighted estimate can be recomputed.

audit.what: Every row the classifier scores 4 or above that the stratified sample had not already covered. Together the two sets are a census of the published region and of the five bands below it, so the published list's precision is counted rather than estimated. The audit was made after the weights were fixed and was not fed back into them.

stratified.what: A probability sample of all 2,629 Annual Plan rows, stratified by sector family crossed with allocation band. This is the only set the threshold sweep uses, because precision and recall estimated on anything else would not generalise to the rows the classifier has not seen.

what: Hand labels for Kerala's Annual Plan rows, a stratified probability sample plus an audit census of everything the classifier scores at or above 4. Ground truth for parse/classify_kerala.py. Audit and correct these: the classifier is only as good as they are.
